messages:
Priya Rao: Customer (AcmeCorp) reports intermittent 401s but says response has no request id header. They pasted the response body only. Asking what to collect so eng can trace.
Sam Bennett: Ask for the exact time window (to the minute) and the client timestamp. Without an ID we need a time range + endpoint + auth header they used.
Priya Rao: Sent back: time range + path + SDK version. Also asked if they can reproduce with curl. They said it's from mobile app and harder to reproduce.
Chris Lee: If mobile, ask them to grab the SDK debug token. For iOS/Android SDKs we log a `debug_token` on init failures — it's in the app logs. Example log line: `RedwoodSDK: debug_token=abc123 token_status=401`.
Priya Rao: Customer says they don't see that string. They only have a generic `Auth failed` in Android logcat.
Sam Bennett: Ok — provide quick adb steps. Ask them to run:

```
adb logcat | grep RedwoodSDK
```

and copy the 10 minutes around the failure.
Priya Rao: Shared that. Also added: if they can do a HAR from the embedded webview or a curl from a laptop that reproduces it, that's best.
Chris Lee: Share a minimal curl they can run (replace placeholders):

```
curl -i -X POST https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate \
  -H "Authorization: Bearer $REDACTED" \
  -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
  -d '{"input":"test"}'
```

Tell them to paste the full response headers so we can find `x-redwood-request-id` or `x-request-id`.
Priya Rao: Asked what to do if the header is missing but they DID call through our SDK.
Chris Lee: Two paths:
- If using a Redwood SDK: ask for the SDK logs (we log request ids and debug tokens). Look for `request_id=` or `debug_token=` entries.
- If using a proxy or private deployment: ask for the proxy logs (location depends on deployment). For on-prem NGINX proxy we typically see `x-redwood-req` in `/var/log/redwood/proxy.log`.
Sam Bennett: Also remind them to redact PII/API keys. We only need headers, timestamps, and request/response bodies (if small).
Priya Rao: Customer can't attach logs due to security. They asked if there's anything in the Console UI they can screenshot.
Chris Lee: Yes — Console -> Requests -> Filter by timeframe -> click the failed request -> the detail pane shows `Request ID`, `Auth status`, and request headers. If they share that Request ID (a short hex string) we're golden.
Priya Rao: Pushed a short checklist for them:
1) exact timestamp (UTC), timezone
2) endpoint path and method
3) full response headers (screenshot or copy)
4) SDK logs around the timestamp (grep for `RedwoodSDK` / `request_id` / `debug_token`)
5) HAR or curl reproduction if possible
6) account/org id and client id (not API key)

SupportBot: :pushpin: Tip: If they provide only a timestamp and path, Eng can search our ingress logs but that becomes noisy if their timeframe is >5m.
Sam Bennett: If this becomes an escalation, include the `debug_token` if available and open a ticket to eng-oncall with the time range + request path + sample header. Tag me and @Chris.
Priya Rao: Customer replied with Android log snippet but obfuscated. It contains `token_status=401` and a UUID-like string not labeled. Can that be a request id?
Chris Lee: Might be our internal attempt id. Ask them to paste the full line. Our request ids look like `req_` prefix or 16-char hex. If uncertain, send the line to eng and we'll parse.
Priya Rao: Also asked if billing/fraud responses can cause missing request ids.
Sam Bennett: Billing/fraud 402/403 responses still include request ids. Missing IDs usually mean the request didn't reach our gateway (client-side failure or proxy stripped header). Check client network logs (DNS, proxy, captive portal).
Chris Lee: Final note for private deployments: if customer is behind a gateway, request id may be injected at the edge. For them, the agent should check edge logs like `edge-proxy` or the `redwood-agent` system journal.
Priya Rao: Thanks—I'm sending the checklist now and asking them to run `adb logcat` and capture the Console Request detail if they can. Will update once they reply.
SupportBot: If you mark this thread as escalation-needed, the escalation workflow will automatically collect the account id and rollout history. :white_check_mark:
